S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear minor to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors or mental acts focused on these concerns and causing significant distress or impairment. Onset is typically in adolescence and early adulthood, often in the context of heightened social comparison, bullying, or appearance-focused environments, and the course is usually chronic without treatment, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress. BDD is distinct from normal appearance dissatisfaction by the intensity of preoccupation, the degree of functional impairment, and the often poor insight or delusional conviction about the perceived defect; it is differentiated from eating disorders by the focus on specific body parts or features rather than weight or shape overall. Comorbidities commonly include depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, and OCD-spectrum conditions, and individuals frequently engage in excessive grooming, mirror checking, reassurance seeking, or camouflaging behaviors, as well as seeking cosmetic procedures that rarely alleviate distress.

patient.personality: Imad is a pragmatic, introverted tinkerer who channels his restlessness into solitary hikes and DIY tech projects while quietly planning for a more responsible future role at work.
patient.stressor: Imad’s concerns about his appearance began to intensify in his final year of high school, when classmates repeatedly made offhand jokes about his looks and he started comparing himself to more athletic peers during gym and on social media. After graduation he moved into a physically demanding warehouse job, where working alongside older, more muscular coworkers in a hot, fluorescently lit environment made him acutely self-conscious about how he looked in his uniform. As he took on more responsibility and talked about pursuing certification, he became increasingly anxious that his appearance would undermine how seriously supervisors and peers viewed him, leading him to spend more and more time before and after shifts trying to “fix” how he looked. The mounting time he devoted to these routines began to interfere with his punctuality, cut into his sleep, and made him turn down social invitations and even extra shifts, prompting him to seek psychiatric help when he realized his attempts to manage his concerns were starting to jeopardize both his job and his plans for advancement.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m spending so much time on these little routines to fix how I look before work that it’s starting to mess with my schedule and my life.”

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: Ever since those jokes in senior year, I can’t stop staring at my face and my build, especially my nose and how skinny my arms look in the warehouse uniform, and it just feels like everyone can see how off and scrawny I am, even when people say they don’t notice anything weird about me.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before every shift I’ll lose like an hour changing shirts, messing with my hair, checking my arms in the mirror from different angles, even doing push-ups and scrolling through gym guys on Instagram to see how bad I look in comparison, and then after work I’ll keep asking my brother if I looked ‘small’ or ‘weird’ all day until he gets annoyed with me.
